'''Ezra Getzler''' (born 9 February 1962 in [[Melbourne]]) is an Australian mathematician and mathematical physicist.

== Education and career ==
Getzler studied from 1979 to 1982 at the [[Australian National University]] in [[Canberra]] (bachelor's degree with honours in 1982). In 1982 he moved to [[Harvard University]] with a [[Fulbright program|Fulbright Scholarship]]; he received his PhD in 1986 under [[Arthur Jaffe]], with a thesis entitled ''Degree theory for Wiener maps and supersymmetric quantum mechanics''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=73854}}</ref>

From 1986 to 1989 he was a [[Harvard Society of Fellows|Junior Fellow]] at Harvard.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Current & Former Junior Fellows |url=https://socfell.fas.harvard.edu/current-former-junior-fellows |access-date=2022-10-16 |website=[[Harvard University]] |language=en}}</ref> He then moved to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he became assistant professor in 1989 and associate professor in 1993. In 1997 he became associate professor at [[Northwestern University]] and since 1999 he is full professor.

He was a guest professor at several universities, including the [[Max-Planck-Institut für Mathematik]] in Bonn (1996), the [[École Normale Supérieure]] (1992), the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] (2007), the [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis]], the [[Imperial College London]] (2007/8), and the [[University of Paris VI]]. In 2002 and in 2003/4 he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/234 Getzler, Ezra — Institute for Advanced Study]</ref>

From 1991 to 1993 a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows Database |url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database |access-date=2022-10-16 |website=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] |language=en}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-03-20.</ref>

== Research ==
Getzler is known for his new proof (1983) of the [[Atiyah–Singer index theorem]] using [[supersymmetry]], based upon ideas of [[Luis Álvarez-Gaumé]] and [[Edward Witten]] in mathematical physics. In addition to [[mathematical physics]], he works on [[algebraic geometry]], [[category theory]], and [[algebraic topology]].

==Works==
* with [[Nicole Berline]], [[Michèle Vergne]], ''Heat Kernels and Dirac Operators'', Springer Verlag, Grundlehren der Mathematischen Wissenschaften, 1992.
* ''Pseudodifferential operators on supermanifolds and the Atiyah–Singer index theorem'', [[Communications in Mathematical Physics]], Vol. 92, 1983, p.&nbsp;163, [http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?service=UI&version=1.0&verb=Display&handle=euclid.cmp/1103940796 Online]
* ''A short proof of the Atiyah–Singer index theorem'', [[Topology (journal)|Topology]] 25 (1987), 111–117.
* ''The local Atiyah–Singer index theorem'', in Konrad Osterwalder, [[Raymond Stora]] (eds.): ''Critical phenomena, random systems, gauge theories'' (Les Houches Lectures 1984), North-Holland, Amsterdam-New York, 1986, pp.&nbsp;967–974. 
* Editor with Mikhail Kapranov: ''Higher category theory'', Workshop Northwestern University 1997, American Mathematical Society 1998.
